findings.title: Default proto codec now rejects APIv1-only messages
findings.why_it_matters: Every RPC whose request or response type implements only the legacy protobuf API (Reset/String/ProtoMessage without ProtoReflect: gogo/protobuf types, code generated by protoc-gen-go < 1.4, hand-written v1 messages such as reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate) now fails with Internal "grpc: error while marshaling: failed to marshal, message is *T, want proto.Message" (and the mirror error on receive). Before, the assertion was against golang/protobuf's proto.Message (the v1 interface) and proto.Marshal wrapped such values via MessageV2; the swapped import makes the same assertion demand ProtoReflect. The stated intent is that the default codec keeps working for existing callers. Converting through protoadapt (already used in internal/status WithDetails in this diff) restores acceptance of both API generations.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a helper in encoding/proto/proto.go and use it in both Marshal and Unmarshal instead of the bare v.(proto.Message) assertion: func messageV2Of(v any) proto.Message { switch v := v.(type) { case protoadapt.MessageV1: return protoadapt.MessageV2Of(v); case protoadapt.MessageV2: return v }; return nil } -- return the existing 'want proto.Message' error when it yields nil. Add a codec test that round-trips an APIv1-only type (e.g. grpc_testing_not_regenerate.SearchRequestV3).
evidence: encoding/proto/proto.go:41 -- vv, ok := v.(proto.Message)   (proto is now google.golang.org/protobuf/proto per encoding/proto/proto.go:27; same assertion repeated at line 49 for Unmarshal)
encoding/proto/proto.go:43 -- return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal, message is %T, want proto.Message", v)

base 5051eeae encoding/proto/proto.go imported "github.com/golang/protobuf/proto", whose Message is protoiface.MessageV1 and whose Marshal calls MessageV2(m) (golang/protobuf@v1.5.3 proto/wire.go:36), so v1-only messages were accepted

reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate/testv3.go is an in-repo APIv1-only generated message set with a registered gRPC service (reflection/serverreflection_test.go:405); it has XXX_ methods and no ProtoReflect
go build ./... and go vet on all changed packages pass at head, so nothing compile-time catches this

findings.title: Status.Details returns internal wrapper for APIv1-only detail types
findings.why_it_matters: Callers that type-switch on status details (case *mypb.ErrorInfo) silently stop matching when the detail type is an APIv1-only registered message: Details() now hands back *impl.messageIfaceWrapper instead of the concrete *T, so error-detail handling falls through to the default branch with no error. The old path used ptypes.Empty, which returned proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()) and therefore unwrapped legacy types to their concrete pointer. protoadapt.MessageV1Of is the identical conversion (both call protoimpl.X.ProtoMessageV1Of), so applying it to the UnmarshalNew result restores the previous dynamic types exactly while leaving APIv2 generated messages untouched.
findings.suggested_fix: In (*Status).Details, append protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail) instead of detail (protoadapt is already imported in this file). For APIv2 generated messages ProtoMessageV1Of returns the same pointer; for legacy wrappers it unwraps to the concrete v1 type, matching the old ptypes.DynamicAny behavior. Add a test with an APIv1-only detail type asserting the concrete type is returned.
evidence: internal/status/status.go:158-163 -- detail, err := any.UnmarshalNew() ... details = append(details, detail)
protobuf@v1.32.0 types/known/anypb/any.pb.go:319 -- dst = mt.New().Interface()
protobuf@v1.32.0 internal/impl/message.go:225-230 -- MessageInfo.New returns mi.MessageOf(m) (a messageReflectWrapper) when the Go type does not implement protoreflect.ProtoMessage
protobuf@v1.32.0 internal/impl/message_reflect_gen.go:140-144 -- messageReflectWrapper.Interface returns (*messageIfaceWrapper)(m) for such types
golang/protobuf@v1.5.3 ptypes/any.go:77 -- return proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()), nil   (old path, unwraps via ProtoMessageV1Of 'case unwrapper')

findings.title: Binary log drops payload of APIv1-only messages
findings.why_it_matters: With binary logging enabled, client and server message entries for APIv1-only message types are now written with Length 0 and no data, and the logger emits "message to log is neither proto.message nor []byte". The type assertion in ClientMessage.toProto and ServerMessage.toProto used to be against the v1 proto.Message interface; after the import swap it requires ProtoReflect, so legacy messages fall through to the unsupported branch and the audit record is silently empty. Checking protoadapt.MessageV1 first and converting with protoadapt.MessageV2Of keeps both generations loggable.
findings.suggested_fix: In both ClientMessage.toProto (line 242) and ServerMessage.toProto (line 282): if m, ok := c.Message.(protoadapt.MessageV1); ok { data, err = proto.Marshal(protoadapt.MessageV2Of(m)) } else if m, ok := c.Message.(protoadapt.MessageV2); ok { data, err = proto.Marshal(m) } else if b, ok := c.Message.([]byte); ok { ... }.
evidence: internal/binarylog/method_logger.go:242 -- if m, ok := c.Message.(proto.Message); ok {   (same at line 282; proto is now google.golang.org/protobuf/proto)
internal/binarylog/method_logger.go:248-250 -- } else { grpclogLogger.Infof("binarylogging: message to log is neither proto.message nor []byte") }
base 5051eeae internal/binarylog/method_logger.go imported github.com/golang/protobuf/proto, whose Message interface v1-only types satisfy

findings.title: Typed-nil messages now marshal as empty instead of erroring
findings.why_it_matters: A handler that returns a nil *Response with a nil error (or a client that passes a nil *Request) used to fail with Internal "grpc: error while marshaling: proto: Marshal called with nil"; it now sends a zero-length message and the peer receives a default-valued message with status OK. golang/protobuf's Marshal explicitly returned ErrNil for invalid (nil-pointer) messages, while google.golang.org/protobuf's Marshal returns nil, nil, and grpc's encode() only filters untyped nils. That converts a loud programming-error signal into silent empty data, which contradicts the behavior-preserving goal for the default codec. Re-adding the IsValid check in the codec restores the old contract.
findings.suggested_fix: In codec.Marshal, after obtaining the v2 message, keep the old contract: if !vv.ProtoReflect().IsValid() { return nil, errors.New("proto: Marshal called with nil") } before proto.Marshal(vv). Assumption: preserving the pre-migration error is desired; if the lenient behavior is intended, document it and add a test pinning it.
evidence: encoding/proto/proto.go:45 -- return proto.Marshal(vv)
golang/protobuf@v1.5.3 proto/wire.go:44-47 -- if len(buf) == len(nbuf) { if !mi.ProtoReflect().IsValid() { return buf, ErrNil } }   (old behavior)

protobuf@v1.32.0 proto/encode.go:74-84 -- Marshal: out, err := MarshalOptions{}.marshal(nil, m.ProtoReflect()); if len(out.Buf) == 0 && err == nil { out.Buf = emptyBytesForMessage(m) } -- returns nil buffer and nil error for an invalid message
rpc_util.go:630 -- if msg == nil { // NOTE: typed nils will not be caught by this check

findings.title: Invalid LRS interval error formats stale nil err
findings.why_it_matters: When the management server sends a missing or out-of-range load_reporting_interval, the returned error reads "invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>" and the actual reason (nil Duration, nanos out of range, sign mismatch) is lost. The rewritten check discards the CheckValid result and formats the outer err from stream.Recv(), which is always nil at this point. Capturing the CheckValid error and formatting it restores the diagnostic the ptypes.Duration version provided.
findings.suggested_fix: rInterval := resp.GetLoadReportingInterval(); if err := rInterval.CheckValid(); err != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }; interval := rInterval.AsDuration()
evidence: xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:174-175 -- if rInterval.CheckValid() != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }
xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:165-168 -- resp, err := stream.Recv(); if err != nil { return ... }   (err is necessarily nil past this point)
base: interval, err := ptypes.Duration(resp.GetLoadReportingInterval()); if err != nil { ... %v, err }

findings.title: Tools module downgrades golang.org/x/tools to v0.14.0
findings.why_it_matters: vet.sh installs goimports from test/tools, so the formatter/import checker used in CI silently moves back from x/tools v0.17.0 to v0.14.0 (with x/sync v0.6.0 -> v0.4.0 and a new x/sys v0.13.0 pin). The immediate base commit is the dependency bump that set v0.17.0, and nothing in a protobuf import migration calls for reverting it, so this looks like a stale conflict resolution rather than an intended change. Keeping the base's x/tools line and only swapping the golang/protobuf requirement for google.golang.org/protobuf avoids running a different tool version than the repo pinned.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore golang.org/x/tools v0.17.0 in test/tools/go.mod (drop the added golang.org/x/sys v0.13.0 indirect line unless tidy re-adds it), keep google.golang.org/protobuf v1.32.0 as a direct requirement, and regenerate test/tools/go.sum with `go mod tidy -compat=1.19` so vet.sh's tidy check stays clean.
evidence: test/tools/go.mod:7 -- golang.org/x/tools v0.14.0   (diff: -golang.org/x/tools v0.17.0 / +golang.org/x/tools v0.14.0; + golang.org/x/sys v0.13.0 // indirect)
vet.sh:36-38 -- pushd ./test/tools ... go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports
provenance: 5051eeae Zach Reyes 2024-01-24 - grpc: Update go mod (#6939) is the review base and the commit that set x/tools v0.17.0 in test/tools/go.mod

residual_risks: Migration is incomplete relative to the stated intent: channelz/service/{service.go,func_linux.go,service_test.go,service_sktopt_test.go}, credentials/credentials.go, xds/internal/xdsclient/bootstrap/bootstrap.go (jsonpb) and internal/pretty/pretty.go (protov1) still import github.com/golang/protobuf, and the root go.mod still requires it directly. No behavior defect follows from this, but the deprecated module is not actually removable yet.

test/tools go.mod/go.sum consistency could not be verified offline (x/tools v0.14.0, honnef and misspell are not in the provided module cache); the hand-edited go.sum drops several /go.mod hashes, so `go install` in test/tools or vet.sh's `go mod tidy` cleanliness check may fail.

Durations that are valid protobuf Durations but exceed time.Duration range (about 292 years) used to be rejected by ptypes.Duration in balancer/rls convertDuration and the LRS interval; they now pass CheckValid and saturate via AsDuration. Low practical impact (RLS max_age is clamped), not raised as a finding.
status.WithDetails with a typed-nil detail used to return an error (v1 Marshal ErrNil) and now appends an empty Any of that type; same root cause as the typed-nil codec finding.

callsite completeness: grep-only -- other `.(proto.Message)` assertions on user-supplied values outside encoding/proto and internal/binarylog were not exhaustively enumerated; nested modules (examples, gcp/observability, interop/observability, security/*, stats/opencensus) were not built.
testing_gaps: No test sends an APIv1-only message (e.g. reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate SearchRequestV3/SearchResponseV3, which already has a registered service in serverreflection_test.go) through the default proto codec, binary logging, or status WithDetails/Details; such a test would have caught the codec regression.
No test covers the LRS first-response path with a missing or invalid load_reporting_interval, so the '<nil>' error text is unobserved.
No test pins the codec's behavior for a typed-nil message (handler returning nil reply with nil error).
